Hi Soojin,

Thanks for walking us through the private deployment options on Friday. The site team in Albuquerque needs a concrete acceptance flow for receiving offline artifacts (USB/SSD courier) and verifying authenticity before loading into the sealed rack. Two quick asks: a) a short checklist the on-site operator can follow for signature and checksum verification, and b) what the fallback looks like if the manifest signature fails during acceptance.

We have constrained network egress and cannot rely on live KMS lookups. Prefer a deterministic, offline verification step.

Can you send a short runbook we can include in the site acceptance packet?

Hi Ben / ACME ops,

Appreciate the detail — attached is a compact acceptance runbook and the proposed offline verification sequence. High-level approach:

1) Signed manifest bundle (PKCS7) travels on the same media as the image.
2) On-site operator validates signature with an embedded root cert bundle (we provide) and confirms SHA256 checksums against the manifest.
3) If signature verification fails, operator quarantines the media and triggers an escalation to the on-call security contact; we provide an encrypted audit token to record the failed attempt in the control plane when the site regains connectivity.

Key constraints and mitigations included in the attached: a short checklist, required operator outputs (screenshot of checksum, manifest serial), and minimal courier receipt fields.

I’ve looped in Marissa for deployment windows and Aditya for signing-process detail.

Thanks,
Soojin
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick operational notes from my side:

• Rollout cadence: we recommend a three-wave staged rollout per site (canary tenant on one rack, regional pilot 10% of fleets, full cutover) with a mandatory 48h verification window between waves.
• Blockers: courier chain-of-custody form must be completed and returned; if that’s missing we pause.
• Operator acceptance window: our on-site playbook assumes a 4hr acceptance window after delivery (arrival + verification). If the site cannot meet that, schedule a different delivery slot.

Ben — attaching a short suggested template for the on-site operator to sign and hold in the sealed-rack log. If the signature in the manifest fails, immediate fallback is: do not install, lock the rack bay (physical tamper), and call the Redwood incident triage line. We will then initiate a remote-forensics packing list to instruct shipping of replacement media via a different courier and signed manifest.

—Marissa

Redwood Inference

Adding technical detail for the offline signature verification flow (brief):

• Signing: release artifacts are signed with our airgap-release key using detached PKCS7. Manifest includes artifact checksums, build metadata, and a manifest serial.
• Root certs: the site receives a root bundle signed by Redwood PKI; the bundle is time-bounded and rotated every 90 days. For offline validation we include a small verification utility (signed binary) on the media to perform: 1) certificate chain verify against the embedded root bundle, 2) checksum comparison, 3) manifest serial sanity checks.
• Escalation token: when signature fails, the utility stamps a locally encrypted audit token (AES-GCM with site-specific wrapping key) that the site can upload when connectivity resumes; token contains timestamp, operator id, and hash of the media. This prevents silent tampering and creates a forward audit record.

I also attach the signed-manifest-v2.json example for your review — this is an example only, not the live artifact.

If ACME wants stronger assurances, we can include an HSM-signed time-stamp in the manifest during packaging. That adds a step on our side but keeps the site offline.

—Aditya
Software & Release Engineer, Private Runtime
Redwood Inference

2) We need the planned root-cert rotation schedule in writing to meet our audit (can you confirm the 90-day rotation and a contact for emergency rotation)?
3) For the fallback courier, can you include the estimated lead time (we have a maintenance window next month and need to schedule accordingly)?

If you can send 1–2 line responses inline, we’ll attach this thread and the checklist to the acceptance packet.

Thanks — Ben
